text: Game Changer Habit is a game changer. The only app of its kind that I have found true success with. I love the beautiful interface and the progress bars in the widgets. If you’re looking to create change and hold yourself accountable, this is the one.

Amazing App This app is very clean and easy to understand interface. Not full of unnecessary information just swipe and the habit is complete. It shows streaks and for more in detail info there is a separate tab for those who like that. Very good app!

Best habit tracker app around This app is really incredible. It let's you customise everything according to your liking. And the best part is it shows you charts and bars of your progress to keep you motivated.

Good but not perfect, and there’s room for improvement 1. No feature to track bad habits; for instance, set goals to limit the time of watching tv or smoking less than three times per week… 2. The tracking timer is a joke. It stops running after it passes a set goal. So it doesn’t care if I do better than my set goal. And no log for the total time I spend on a timed habit. 3. The arrangement of the complete buttons on the Apple watch is not intuitive. For example, after drinking a cup of water, I need to hit a tiny button while the big green check button is for completing all cups a day. Who can drink like 7 cups in one seat? 4. It is difficult and not satisfying to hit the complete button in the app. For example, after drinking a cup of water, I need to slide a bit on the complete button to increase one, not just by taping.

This app changed my routine!! This habit tracking app is a game-changer! It's so user-friendly and customizable. You can set up your habits and track them daily, weekly, or monthly. The app also allows you to set reminders, so you never forget to complete a habit. The visual representation of your progress is motivating and keeps you accountable. Overall, this app has helped me stay on track with my goals and has improved my daily routine.

Yes I needed something to track my daily habits and this is exactly what I was looking for. The option to share will allow me stay accountable to my mentor. Excited to see the charts fill up and to have new habits become automatic like brushing my teeth.

God’s calling for this season I had been trying to become disciplined in the self care I wanted to do. I knew I needed some help. I use Habit to track all the daily activities I need to accomplish. These things need to happen daily. It’s so helpful to be able to track what I’ve completed and what needs to get finished for the day. I love that I can see my day streaks, and my progress. Every time I swipe on a task, I feel fulfillment. I’m putting together a 30 day recap of this month of deep self restoration and I’m including screen recordings of me using the app along the way. I even have a widget of my tasks on my Home Screen. I love Habit. We should work together (:

Good but quirky Widget click does not open the specific habit Simple one tap click on habit to add one is not possible Reducing by swiping not possible UI little to complicated. Awesome Habits can do the same but with way less buttons Price is way better than Awesome habits. If the widget thing would be fixed it would insta buy this

Perfect except for loss of sound?! I love this app, my only critique is that sound sometimes stops working. Even when sound is activated and I’ve checked my iPhone volume settings etc. it’s annoying as I love the sound when you swipe to say you’ve done a task - it motivates me

Amazing - highly recommend I hace adhd and a routine is very important I love using this to keep track of all my habits with the widget on my screen. It is nice to see a visual representation of the streaks. This app has helped me establish and maintain the habits I want to keep up with.

Highly recommended It has transformed my daily routine for the better. The user-friendly interface makes it a breeze to set up and monitor my habits. The reminders are a game-changer, helping me stay on track effortlessly. Plus, the visual progress charts are incredible. Highly recommended!

Obliged to Davetech This app is just the perfect combination of a todo list as well as a habit tracker. Best part, it even has a slider/progress bar type thingy that one can slide to increase the count of sub tasks completed, which i find very helpful. In addition, the app even has integrated graphs for a very quick review of the progress. By and large, its really good. You should give it a try :)

Best App in its category. So easy to keep track and develop any new habit with the help of this app. The graph and all the visual representation of the habits is such a major boost. additionally, the UI is so simple yet it looks soo elegant. Well deserving 🌟🌟🌟🌟🌟

Wow! So glad I found this app. I downloaded 4 free apps to see which ones best fits my brain for my new goal tracking. I absolutely love this one! The look is clean and not too busy plus you can create your own color schemes that are pleasing to you. It connects with your Apple Health and automatically tracks when you completed the goal. So far mines are all fitness related but I will be doing some personal / work goals and tracking them manually. There is a widget for the watch face as well. Quick way to swipe for complete goals without being distracted with the phone.

Nice app overall I have used many habit tracking apps but I feel this is the best one so far. With different color coding and emojis, it does have really nice UI/UX design. It also allows us to select a style which soothes our eyes. I also like that it is optional to create reminders. I am not sure if this feature is already there but it would be nice if they had checkbox kind of thing as an option with slider because I like clicking the checkboxes rather than using the slider. I don’t know why but I find it more satisfying. I also wish they had kept adding habits feature free.

Game changer I love the simple layout of this app - really aesthetically pleasing and very few visual distractions. I love the widget on my home screen as it is a constant reminder to do my daily tasks/habits and v satisfying to see the full bars when I have completed them. Brilliant for folk who struggle with developing new habits, or just struggle with staying on track eg adhders

Great App The free version includes the necessities to track your habits which I’ve been doing for 2 months. Super satisfying intuitive layout, particularly with widgets - love seeing full bars for some reason. Also one thing I love about this app is memos. I write reflections of each of my habits and feel that I gain insight to myself. If that makes sense. Great app love it, thank you devs for premium 🫶🏼

Best app ever!!!! I absolutely LOVE HABIT!!!!!! The app is simple to use, just the right amount of interactive use, easy on the eyes. A complete all rounder for me!!! I have adhd and dyslexia, so this app is a simple and effective way to get my daily tasks done which I love! I hate apps with too many features or too much design or contrasting colours. To complete tasks you can tick or slide, I prefer the sliding because it helps my sensory issues. I’m also a Uni student trying to get in some consistency in my day to day routine, and habit seems to motivate me to do that because it’s simple and easy to create, check off and edit tasks. There’s also this adorable mood tracker which I love even more because I usually journal down stuff in a diary, but sometimes I just can not be bothered, but I regret it later so the little mood tracker is adorable in letting me be consistent in writing down my moods/feelings all in one app!!! Also keeps track of ur consistency in habit completion and gives u a cute little ‘🔥’ streak on habits which are done for whatever frequency u set it for. If I have not made it clear already, I love this app! Thank you so much for the scholarship as well Habit!
Great Great app, allows you to perfectly visualise your progress

Amazing app, and a couple of suggestions! I love this app a lot, definitely the habit app with the best price! I only request more apple watch syncing, if possible! Being able to track specific exercises and have it read the minutes done from the health app would be immensely beneficial (yoga, pilates, etc). The app already has some activities synced, but more would be sooooo useful! I would also prefer a way to press a button to immediately mark an activity as done instead of swiping, it would be a lot faster!

Great app, but could be better on Apple Watch This is a really great app and does everything you could want from a habit app imo. The interface is great and so is the customisation. However, it’s really disappointing that on the Apple Watch when you complete a habit the whole item isn’t coloured in like it does on the phone app, it’s only a small bar along the bottom to show you’ve completed it. Hard to see on the watch face, and harder to feel the accomplishment when it’s hard to tell if it’s been completed or not!

Phenomenal App Like the title says, this app is phenomenal. It’s a great way to track progress on a habit you’re trying to get down. I’ve used it to develop a skincare routine, read more, exercise more consistently, and keep track of medications I’ve taken throughout the day. I find it incredibly satisfying to close a habit too. I also enjoy the app’s emphasis on stats. Each time you close the little habit bar, it adds to your current streak. They have stats readily available and a multitude of charts and graphs to keep up with your habits. And it’s easy to customize too. You can play with the app’s icon and colors, habit colors, in app colors and pretty much anything else in the app. There’s a vacation mode too, where it’ll skip habits automatically within a timeframe you set. And there’s a bunch of features I’m sure I missed. The app can work with Apple’s health app and keep up with your steps for you to see if you’re meeting your goal, which is convenient if you track everything else in the app. And the app tries to prevent cheating as much as possible. Like you can’t check off a future habit for instance. Would definitely recommend if you want to start some routines and need a way to keep up with your progress.

Super helpful This app has helped me visualize what my day looks like in little bits. It’s fun to swipe that I’ve finished something for the day. I really like the feature that allows you to put that you’ve only partially done something so that you can be reminded that you’ve let’s say, only walked for 30 min out of 1 hour.

Very easy to use I think this is a really great app for helping me remember my daily tasks. It’s very easy to do. Very simple layout with nice colors. It doesn’t require a lot of clicking and selecting other apps. Just a swipe and it’s done.

Best app there is to find ! Omg , This habit tracker app helps me to stay accountable and motivated towards my goals through visual progress tracking, reminders and notifications, goal setting and milestones, data analysis and insights, social engagement, and customization. By providing a comprehensive and tailored experience, this app empowers me to stay on track, make progress, and achieve my desired outcomes , Omg not to mention they give me perineum for free , I couldn’t say thank you enjoy and show my gratitude and appreciation, I’ve never came across an app that has a option why you couldn’t afford something or to help you , Never , the absolutely beautiful kind people who designed this are amazing people and such kind individuals that understand it’s hard for people so they give a opportunity that is so kind and so unlike like other apps , as an 18 year old struggling with life I couldn’t say enough thank you and thank you for letting people have an option if they couldn’t afford something due to their financial situation . I couldn’t recommend this app enough! And I would absolutely pay if I could and when I am financially stable I’ll definitely pay ! I’ll give all of my money to support such amazing people! This is the best app out their you’ll find ! .

The best app for habit tracking I love the way how you close your daily habit by swiping the bar, also widgets can show your progress and it keeps you active and focus. Thx, one more thing: simple app and easy to use. I can say to the developers of this app: Great job guys , awesome work and great program.

This is the Best tracking tool out there I bave used almost 10 apps to find the best fit. This is hands-down the best. The graphs are really helpful and you can just swipe to track things. Also, you can customize reminders and memos which enable complete control.

This App Has MADE MY LIFE EASIER😭😭 I absolutely cannot stress enough how much it has helped me stick to my habits. I used to make a to do list on paper but i forget anything thats not in front of my eyes. So i downloaded this. Its very easy to use. I love sliding habits when i have done them. I absolutely love the mood tracker. Added a widget of it also on my homescreen. App interface and overall built is also very pleasant like its not too much that i get confused and it has colors which makes it exciting to use. I absolutely love my Habit App! 😍😍😍🥰🥰🥰🥰🥰🥰 I am drinking more water, i am doing 4 hours work, i even put a habit to play with my cat lol its soo gooood. Helping me become a better person everyday. I am so thankful 😘😘😘😘😘😘😘
Totally recommend User friendly app, it helps me to build positive habits and break bad ones. It provides visual feedback on your progress and makes tracking daily habits a breeze.
A really good habit tracker Features are easy and intuitive to use Beautiful graphs, progress bars, timer and pixel visualisation

My favorite habit tracking app!!! I absolutely LOVE this app. I’ve tried a lot of habit tracking apps and this one is by far my favorite!! The timers are so helpful and something about completing a task and sliding the little bar over is sooo satisfying. I also love the widgets and little icons and colors for each task.
Nice colors Nice colors and swipe interface which is enjoyable to use

The best I love that habit tracker has an option for you to pled your case as to why you want premium. I am a very busy mom of 2 under 2 and it is soooo difficult for me to put time and energy into myself, but the habit app allows me to keep a visual representation of what I have completed so I do not forget with my unhinged pp brain.
Very helpful It really helps me to track my habits. It has great structures, love the swiping! Great app!!
Best habit tracker out there The best habit tracker app I’ve found. Functions well, satisfying to swipe and the colour schemes are pleasing to the eye

Helpful and Fun It's so helpful to be able to track stuff from your phone. It also makes me more apt to get my goals done each week cause I can't cope with a half filled circle each week (which also helps me adjust to make my goals more realistic). Plus I made a daily goal of "be hot" and every day I complete it and get a little confetti screen - 10/10 daily affirmation, highly recommend.
A perfect, necessary app. This app unlocked a need I didn’t know I had. It’s fun to swipe tasks I’ve completed. It makes getting daily things done almost entertaining and like a game.

Amazing App Only reason this isn’t a 5 star is there are some minor things I think could improve it, like having a fortnightly habit option or selecting specific days in the month (every first Sunday instead of the 7th, that sort of thing). That and maybe a little plus sign on some of the habits rather than trying to swipe or taking the time to type +1 would be nice lol… but if these are the only criticisms I have then this app really is great and absolutely recommend!! Download it!!

Amazing app This app is a fantastic tool for building and maintaining positive habits. Its user-friendly design, customizable reminders, and visual progress charts make tracking habits effortless and motivating. Highly recommended for boosting productivity and consistency!

Generally good Though it is way to easy to accidentally make wrong input to your habits, and you cannot un-make that. Simply a touch on the widget on the screen, or a little swipe in the app, made my reading hours record gone wrong and this happened every once in a while.

SO GOOD i never write reviews but i wanna help anyone else with adhd who wants to build better habits. this app is so good, i love when apps have a one time small payment that’s worth it instead of a stupid subscription. this app UI can be a tiny bit confusing at first but it’s SUPER customizable so you can make it align with your preferences. it’s really motivating to customize your own habits and how they appear and then swiping them when you complete them. it also has daily emotional check ins where you select how you’re feeling and can leave a little memo. you can also get the memo option to pop up after completing a habit, which i disabled for a lot of my habits but kept on for my gym habit, which i use to track what i hit at the gym so i can see my progress and growth. i really think this app is gonna help me a lot!!! i def recommend:)

Great app! Went for premium. It’s been helping me with my goals and I love it. My only request is that we can choose between swiping a task and checking it off (with a check mark). It sounds weird but I don’t like the swipe.

Un véritable coup de cœur J’ai acheté la version premium sur un coup de tête pour la modique somme de 3,99€. Je ne pensais pas l’utiliser quotidiennement. Belle, simple, efficace, c’est l’une de mes applications préférées (de tous les temps, oui oui). Ce que j’adore : • le design • les statistiques détaillées (représentations visuelles de la tâche durant l’année ou la semaine par exemple, durée totale consacrée à la routine) • la possibilité de « skip » (sauter) des jours sans perdre le « streak » (nombre de jours consécutifs, source de motivation) quand on ne peut vraiment pas consacrer de temps à la tâche • le chronomètre (ou le minuteur, au choix) dont l’utilisation se répercute sur la tâche lorsqu’on l’utilise (on voit que la barre de progression se remplit donc on voit notre avancée) Ce que j’aime moins (bon OK, ce que je DÉTESTE) : • le fait de ne pas pouvoir définir une date de fin le jour même (exemple : je viens de terminer un livre, je veux définir la fin de la routine aujourd’hui avant de l’archiver mais non… je dois définir la date de fin au jour du lendemain, faussant les statistiques), je trouve ça idiot… • un petit bug de son de rien du tout (le son qui ne se lance pas pendant le minuteur mais il faut juste le sélectionner à nouveau, je chipote… parce que oui, on peut choisir des sons de nature par exemple) Sinon, je la recommande haut la main… enfin haut le pouce !!!

What Tony the Tiger didn’t say It’s a “Go-o-ood” app. Had it for idk how long— maybe 3-4 years now, but it’s done it’s job. It’s had a few bugs through that time, some seriously annoying but nothing that made me hate it. Personally, I’m not long term goal oriented, I do things that find me joy in the now and this sorta helps seeing those lil day blocks fill in. A lot of the times I fall out of the habit and forget about doing anything in general, but this— get you a chicken salad.

Bug I have a habit of doing 100 push ups a day. I want to drag a slider to add 20 push for example. It doesn’t allow me to do it. Instead it’s only 0 or 100. I can do it by tapping + button a bunch of times but it’s very inefficient.

Makes Habits fun I genuinely love this app so much. I bought Premium Version and I don't regret it for a second! It's so fun to put in Habits, the colors and see your streak as your fill them out everyday. It even has vacation mode which makes you focus on living and not just being obsessed with Habits. 🩷😍

Hey Hey your app is very good but i can say that the indicators are very very very bugged, also its very hard to find which habitindicator increases with entering digits and which is sliding etc, also they always gonna be bugged. when i click the widget it automatically completes the thing sometimes but not everytime. this makes me to not use the app continiouslu in my subconcious i guess because this app is great for people especially have adhd or typelike. and cant using the app easily makes me feel uncomfortable. Also in the habits special adjusting panel, i always press wrong buttons cause they are all different specifications. trying to make app detailed is great but minimalicity is more important i guess. the app is very minimal but the settings aren’t. hope you guys see it and make it more like apple’s inovative minimalistic style more.

Points for improvement Quite promising app, however still some important thing missing for me. I am giving a 1 star, so the development team would notice my points for improvement. Later I can change my rating. - Not possible to set habbit as YES/NO goal. - Not possible to set „clock“ goal value. E.g. „wake up before 7.00 a.m“. - Not possible to set a range for a goal value. E.g. „sleep duration between 7 to 9 hours“. - Not possible to distinguish between the 0 value and „not filled value“ for a habit. I want to see blank „spot“ if I do not fill up anything, and if the value is really 0, I want to „confirm“ that first. - If a „build“ habit is not fulfilled, I want to see it marked with „cross“, the same way as when a „quit“ habit is not met. Instead the habit is marked with a lighter color than if it was fulfiled. It is confusing and not clear. - I want to have the habits sorted as I want and if I complete any, I want this habit to move to the bottom of the list. I cannot do that. I can switch to „Bottom“ mode, but the list is not sorted as I want, but splitted into „Quit“ and „Build“ sections.

Great value Thanks for the new update! Trying to slide all the time was getting annoying! I use this app everyday and it’s genuinely improving my life. However I really wish there were some changes to the sharing habits section. Everytime me and my partner want to add a new habit together we have to send the sms link. It would be nice if we could do it direct on app. ❤️❤️

Unusable since update Have been using this app for years now with no issue, unfortunately ever since it updated a few days ago the option to swipe to complete/part complete tasks has been removed. Going into each individual task is very time consuming. There doesn’t seem to be a way to revert to the old version of the app as promised when I accepted the update. This renders the app unusable for me.

Why cancel the slide option with the HabitBat button (which is very useful when running)?! The slide option was particularly useful when running and tracking the distance without having to enter the habit and add it manually. What a waste of time now! Definitely a downgrade in UX.
I love this app!! Thank you for the promo! But please bring back the slider to input data on each habit. Thanks! Review update: Thank you for bringing the slider back. That was fast!💖

Lots of bugs Considering I paid $8.99 I thought the app would be extremely robust with no bugs. Some things I encountered in the first 20 minutes of using the app that I would like to be fixed: - the first time I added a custom habit it didn’t appear on the home page. I had to reload it by closing out of the app completely and reopening it. - the slider intervals don’t adhere to the intervals I inputted in the “HabitBar Gesture” “add here” text entry box. In addition, the “x” to delete the pre-typed value is difficult to see, which is extra frustrating since you can’t delete the pre-typed value (of numbers with decimal values e.g. 0.02 hours) with the delete button on the keyboard. There is also no decimal point button on the keyboard so you can’t set the interval to non-whole numbers (e.g. 0.5 hours). Some more issues with the swipe right to check in feature but there’s just too many things wrong with it to list. Some of the ui is a little confusing, such as the mood tracker being a modal only accessible by the small emoticon in the upper right corner of the home page. I’ve only had the app for less than an hour trying to set up my habits, so I haven’t started actually tracking habits and been able to run into any bugs unrelated to setting up the habits. I do like how the app looks and works so I hope these issues can be fixed!
Good and improving I want to focus on one point: tapping a progress bar should increment it, not necessarily complete it. If there's a setting for this I don't know where it is.
Habit Gesture Driving Me Nuts After creating a habit over 20 count, the gesture doesn’t let you slowly swipe right by increments below 5. Please allow increments of 1
Eh Meh, it keeps track of what I need it to and this would have been five stars but now that I can't slide progress on the bars on the go and have to manually add to my habits it kinda sucks.

Issue with swipping I have always added a part of my goal (ex: 7hrs of sleep of an 8hr goal by partially swipping). The option does not seem to be able to be configured anymore. I spent 20 minutes trying to configure it and it’ not possible. Worst UX in history and I paid premium.

Swipe to check in I dont know what happened to the swipe to check in because its what ive always used but its now become so annoying. when you try to swipe if your are not perfect it will bring up this annoying pop up where it tells you to type in a number of hours times or etc. The swipe to use used to be my favorite it was the easiest and fastest to interact with and now its unusable. I dont want to have to click several buttons just to say that I finished something. The entire app has also gotten so laggy and slow. Buying the lifetime premium has been the biggest waste of money and my biggest regret.

Loss of Feature FIXED! I am so happy to have that feature back. Thank you So much! The link for support is still weird, if you can sort that. Hello, please fix the loss of the feature where you could swipe partway through, when you finished part of a habit. I have restarted my phone and it is still “all or nothing” which I find frustrating, as I liked and used that feature. I tried to use “App Support” and the link went to a weird page. Putting 1 star to get attention and changing once fixed. Thank you.

I really like this app but… Recently the widgets(which is the main way i interact with tha app) have been glitching every time u tap the widget to open the app it fills whatever task u tap to 100%. It’s very annoying. I really hope it gets fixed soon

Overall good but it’s also changed I have used this app since April 2023 and it has been very helpful in tracking habits and goals. I recommend it but with some reservations. About a month ago my daily streak numbers were all messed up. I don’t know what changed. An update? I have two habits that were over 1000 days and now they were down to just over 160. Also when a habit is completed for the day it will no longer fill in the bar. I have to open the previous day and then go back to today for it to complete. A month ago I would have given 5 stars, but unless these issues are fixed I am barely giving it 3 stars.

Used to be a great app, not anymore This used to be a great app. I’ve been using it for a couple of years and it always worked so well. But lately, it’s been extremely glitchy. When I click on the habit to complete it, the bar won’t fill in. The developer seems to be chasing problems by putting new updates out to fix the issues, but it will help for only a short time and then new issues will arise or existing issues will come back. I’m having more issues today and looked for an update, and there is none. I’m getting really sick of this app now, and I’m mad I paid for it. I used to love it. Won’t be using this anymore and will be looking for a new app. I suggest you do the same.

Widget Widget functionality is still a mess. Doesn’t recognize tap increments and just adds in random values. Works for a couple of hours and then some bars reset or some get marks done.. seems to be an issue with opening the app and leaving in the background, but even that doesn’t fix it. Yes removed widget and restarted and still keeps occurring. Makes widget functionally useless

Is there an area for journaling ? So far I really like the layout and the satisfaction of swiping goals when completed! I just downloaded yesterday and am curious if the memos get saved each day so I can use it as a journal to keep track of mood and thoughts during this process? Thanks !

User Friendly Tool that Keeps Us Productive! This habit tracker is user friendly for me AND my tween daughter! It is very simple to setup/customize/edit habits! We love the sound effects & progress bars to keep us on track with that extra hit of dopamine, too! We really appreciate the skip feature, so our streaks across the weeks and months are not totally reset. This app functions smoothly and has been an excellent tool to accomplish so many goals!

Overall it’s good Not too complex, not too simple, nice balance. I wish the mood records were improved, because the interface behaves weird - when I click on my moods from the past month I would expect to see my memos. Also widget sometimes behaves erraticaly, filling the unintended goals.

Amazing great for adhd Really incredible app. I love not only how useful and easy it is to use and all the reminders and all the different types of tracking, including mood (the ability to leave notes on everything, and export the data!) but also how visually appealing it is as well. It’s an amazing app and really helps with my ADHD because I get to cross off the main things I want done every day and the Reminders really do help. I also really appreciate the Habit tracking and how the meter also fills up as you go. Please don’t ever discontinue.

The best so far! Well after a couple of weeks solid testing I really like this app. It is now my go-to Habit app. Believe it or not, there aren't that many "good" habit apps out there. And this one really shines. And there are some great hidden features like swiping gestures with the app. Having multiple reminders is essential and they work great. And the notifications are really funny too. Great sense of style. As of now I really can't think of any improvements that could be made at this time. Keep it simple and fast

Great app! This app is perfect for me. Great design and colours. You finish tasks with a right swipe which is very intuitive. Perfect set of features and you get a 1-month free trial for premium! This app is the best one to use with friends. You can compare each other’s progress and motivate each other! Also, you & your friends get a 3-month trial if they use your code after downloading the app. I noticed a bug tho. In some shared habits with friends, my streak just shows 0 even after I’ve had multiple entries. Please try to fix this. Other than that.. GREAT GREAT APP. Love it!

Great app! & really motivational!!! I actually love this app, I’ve been looking for a good habit app for a long time, and this one is just simple to use and I love that it’s just there all together in on page. The colours and the mini emoticon images help to keep you motivated! And I especially really enjoy the sliding bars, that you can drag them to tick off stuff. I will 100% keep using this app because it’s just simply amazing!

Good Visuals I’m enjoying this Habit Tracker over some of the other ones available because (in my opinion) it has more pleasing visual trackers. I especially like the function that lights up little boxes to show you how often you’ve done that habit during the entire year.
Took away the feature! Please bring back the ‘slide to inch towards completion’ on the intuitive mode!!!

Amazing habit tracker I am really satisfied with the functionality of the app, especially that it uses iPhone data to automatically track some habits. I think it would be even better, if it was possible to see progress of weekly tasks, if the bar was visually divided into sections by reps (e.g. Two out of three reps in a week accomplished, therefore two sectioned are highlighted and third one remains empty). Just an idea :)

Great app! This is the best app to track what you want to do as a habit daily, weekly and monthly. And it’s free. Custom habits, color schemes and icons are perfect and simple. I love that I can slide to record habits. Crashes sometimes but looks like they’re fixing the bugs. I use this app everyday. Keep it up! Awesome app. After trying many habit apps, I found this as the most useful. Cheers!

I love this app I was using Habitify before but some recent changes to it broke it completely for me so I gave this one a chance and it paid off! I love the UI, the dashboard overview etc. One thing I’d love to change is the size of the habbit marking buttons — at the moment they span almost the whole screen which makes swiping the habits a bit unwieldy on iPhones with large screens. Other than that this app is wonderful!

I love this app I love this app. It’s pretty well laid out - fairly simple - and I love the color options. Good, but needs some UX/UI improvements. I will also mention that the level of color customization and widgets is so much fun - I loved making it my own style as I was adding tasks! But the UX/UI feels like it was made for an iPhone 5. Instead of natural swiping motions (as many people use to read books on their phone, scroll Tiktok and Twitter), this app has specific, small areas of the screen that have to be tapped precisely to navigate parts of the app. Namely, on the 4th “tab” Calendar Icon of the habit tracker. I have to press the tiny arrows next to the week when I want to see week-by-week progress, but my thumb naturally wants to swipe to get there. It gets a bit frustrating to precisely tap my finger while holding my phone, and made me notice how useful apps that I can navigate one-handed are. (Also, this 4th tab is very middle-school graphic design vibes with the sun and moon. It’s cute, but it just looks old and dated on an iPhone 13. I would lean towards modernizing this.) Also, on the 1st “tab” with the plus sign, it would be useful to see upcoming tasks for tomorrow (similar to Reminders), because I sometimes have to do a task one-day early (laundry before going out of town, etc). That swiping motion for completion is super useful. Just need the ability to swipe between days here too!! A consistent existing button at the bottom of the app to add a habit would be good too - I personally don’t see much value in the 3rd Tab “Group” as I live alone. A button to quick-add a habit would be much more useful to me, but maybe that’s personal preference! I will continue to use, but I will be really, truly satisfied with my purchase if updates like the above come down the line.

Filling circles is fun! When I looked at habit-forming apps back in 2016, I didn't even consider Streaks [$4, iOS]. This is because the app limited you to six habits you could track. No premium, in-app purchase would increase or remove that limit. After habit building for the past year, though, I've come to agree with the app's developer: trying to concentrate on more than six habits at a time is difficult. They wisely chose this limit to help users focus. Or maybe it's because only six rings fit comfortably on one screen. Streaks' unique interface has you tap and hold on a habit to indicate completion; a cute animation completes the ring and fills in the circle to show your progress. The app uses the same UI on its Today widget, offering a super quick method for tracking your progress. Frankly, those two features make Streaks the easiest of these apps to use and the most fun. But I still find some downsides to using the app. One is that the app is just willy-nilly with its reminders. You can't set what times *you* want to be reminded of your habit; instead, the app remind you whenever *it* feels like it. Another is the lack of tracking for negative habits, those which you want to break. And while you *can* track habits that require multiple completions per day, you can't log the number of completions above a set amount; for example, I can't track how many times I sent a card above my goal of two times a day. Finally, there is no way to skip a day without breaking a streak. But if these issues don't matter to you (and, for many, they won't) or if you like the idea of auto completing habits that are Health-related, Streaks is a fine app.

Nice, could’ve better Don't get me wrong. I like the Streaks app. Enough so that I purchased both Streaks and Streaks Workout. But… I used them for a few months when I first purchased them, gave up when their shortcomings got too annoying, and have now, 6 months later, decided to try giving Streaks another try. It's marginally better than the first time, but still has frustrating limitations. I would gladly switch to another app but have not yet found a better one. :-( First, Streaks is a "Seinfelder" app - a habit tracker/trainer that is supposed to work by inspiring you to "Don't break the chain", by making a nice big colorful mark on your calendar when you have done the wanted habit on a particular day, and a big X when you have not done so. Inspired by Jerry Seinfeld's advice on how to develop a practice. Streaks is okay as a Seinfelder app. It provides a calendar for each of the 12 habits. However, it does not provide a unified calendar, where you can see all of the habits in the same calendar box. Strange, since Streaks has nice colorful icons for each habit. Also, Streaks does not manage to export these completion indications to Google or iCloud calendars the way similar apps do. Streaks supports "negative" habits. For example, one of my negative habits is "Eating Bad Food" and "Breaking My Diet". A negative habit starts off brightly colored and complete, and turns into an X if you admit to breaking the chain. So far, so good. But, there are really 3 states here: (0) have not yet messed up, (1) messed up, X, and (3) got to end of day without messing up. In the calendar view, these three states are a hollow circle, an X, and a filled circle, respectively. But in the main app view state (0) have not yet messed up is confusingly indicated by the same full color icon that indicates successful completion for a positive task. Streaks allows you to say that you want to do N repeats of a task per day. E.g. I may want to stretch my injured shoulder twice a day, morning and night. And get bonus points if I also stretch at lunch. But Streaks does not understand "bonus points" - it stops counting after your minimum goal is reached. Streaks does not understand that while you may want to "Keep the chain going" any day you complete more than one such task, but that you may also want to TRACK how many times you performed the task. Finally: the big issue: Streaks only supports 12 tasks. 2 groups of 6. In separate iPhone screens that you must hit a non-intuitive button to switch between. I actually prefer the Apple Watch app for streaks, which allows me to swipe and scroll. Note how I called Streaks a habit tracker/trainer? Streaks is probably right in that you can really only TRAIN a small number of habits at a time. One or two. But you can TRACK more things easily. Note that I said "track THINGS", not "track HABITS". Indeed, TRAINing a single habit may involve TRACKing several things. E.g. my sore shoulder: I want to TRAIN the stretching habit to eliminate shoulder pain. So I would like to TRACK shoulder pain, to see if it is less on days that I have stretched. Ditto, RMS "computeritis". I.e. I want to TRACK 2 symptoms, to see if they are improved by TRAINing the habit. And, for that matter, the see if the time of day I do my stretches correlates to the amount of pain. If you say that Streaks is only about training and not tracking - well, it is that much less useful because of that limitation. Hence my seeking a better app. Small Stuff It is good that Streaks has an Apple Watch app. One of the main reasons I tried Streaks again. Streaks supposedly does voice commands using Siri voice Shortcuts, on iPhone and Watch. This worked for about 2 hours, then broke with "Sorry, there was a problem with the app". Can't blame Streaks fir this, many folks report this problem with Siri voice Shortcuts. Streaks' iPhone app interface is pretty, but strange, non-intuitive, and inconsistent. E.g. it doesn't swipe between screens. E.g. X is used for accept changes and return in some places, whereas Done is used in other places. Streaks supports "Do task once every N days", etc. But it does not support "Do task at least M times every N days". I may want to do something at least once or twice a day, but I may want to count how many times I have done it. I.e. count for “don’t break the chain” and count for tracking should be separate. More and more I am making all Streaks items at least count 2 per day. States are 0 - haven’t done anything, 1 did some, and 2 did enough, met or exceeded my goal

A quick request for new widgets Love this app, use it all the time. Elegant and clean, highly motivating. On a day where I am doing both tasks, the weekly one fills up half the bar in the widget and the daily one fills up the other half in three increments. This is as expected. However, on a day where I am only doing my 3x daily task I would expect them to fill up the entire circle in three increments since I do not have my 3x weekly task scheduled on that day. (It is scheduled for Sunday, Tuesday, Thursday). However it currently is only filling up the same amount of space as on a day where I have both tasks. So on a Monday for example, I complete my 3x daily tasks but the progress bar on the widget only appears half full as though expecting me to complete the 3x weekly task which is not scheduled for that day. When I go into the actual app that task appears faded, yet the widget shows me that my tasks are incomplete. Would love to see this functionality update dynamically based on how many tasks are scheduled that day, not just all tasks regardless of how many need to be completed that day.

Great app, except for weekly goals. Daily and automated health-based habits work great. Main complaint is just the confusing way weekly goals are set up. For example, you can only select failed/success for entire week, but cannot log completed on Mon, Wed and Thursday. The stats for weekly tasks seem buggy, too. Finally, the “completed” dot does not fill If you are on track for a weekly task. For example, if you are 2 days into the week, have logged habit both days, and have a goal of 5 logs/week, the task will remain incomplete, reminding you that you are behind, even though you’re not. Best by far but needs more First of all this app is overall fantastic. I’ve been using it daily to keep myself on task with so many goals and habits, from drinking water to practicing my second language, meditating, exercising, reducing alcohol and even going to bed earlier. The devs have done such a great job. Thank you for an awesome app! Having said that there are a few things I notice that make the app a bit less useful than it could be for me, and sometimes downright annoying: 1. Bonus time/counts — we NEED to be able to track when we go above and beyond our goal for a task! If I reach my 10 glasses of water/day and get in 2 more I wanna record that! If I hit my 6 hours for waist training and squeeze out another hour I want that credit! Think of how well this could play into weekly/monthly goals. Maybe one day I can only do 5 hours but another I can do 7. I’m still on track for a weekly target but presently if I don’t hit exactly 6 every day I’ve effectively accomplished nothing. Not awesome. Right now I use multiple habits for bonus time but it’s a wonky workaround. On that note there definitely need to be tasks set up as weekly or monthly targets from the get go, so we can continue recording a single streak across multiple days if all someone cares about it hitting a longer-term total target. 2. Better timer syncing. Right now if you start a timer on your phone your watch and iPad will show no progress until you pause it on the original device. If it’s still running on the original device and you start it on a second one cuz you forgot where you started it and think you forgot to start it altogether you risk erasing your progress altogether. This is a big one. Timers need to start and show in-progress time on all devices regardless of where they’re started. 3. More pages! Especially needing to add extra habits to track when I surpass my goals 12 is just not enough. Even without my “hacks” I was at 9. Why the limit? Tbh I’m not even sure pages is the best UI. Maybe just a scrolling vertical screen like on the watch? 4. The tap-and-hold UI on iPhone/iPad is not the best and it’s quite glitchy. I frequently have to do it more than once after an entry just fails to log. The circle fills up and then erases itself - animation and all! Really frustrating. The apps should all function like they do on the watch. A simple tap adds the increment. Tap and hold can open each habit to its own screen where its calendar can be modified and data viewed. Nobody needs that tiny little 2nd and 3rd screen behind the habit circle you need to enlarge first to actually use anyway. 5. Widgets and complications need help. Timers and progress are all over the place and literally never reliable. The actual time only displays 20% of the time in the widget and it’s so small even I can barely read it and I’m the weirdo who keeps her phone’s text size as small as it goes. 6. There needs to be a way to edit increments or time (for timed tasks) after the fact. If you mess up recording progress you’re basically screwed for that day. If a task has 10 increments (like my water goal) and I drink 4 glasses at once after a workout, tapping a holding 4 times to notch that up is a chore. We need to be able to bring up the habit screen and just notch up multiple increments using a dial or numerical entry. Same goes TRIPLE for timed tasks. Normal tasks worst case can be reset and manually ticked up again but if you forget to pause a timer there’s just no way to correct your day’s progress so it’s a total wash for the day. That’s kind crazy.

For the Medically Challenged I never leave reviews. Ever. But this app has helped change my life. I'm 37, have extreme ADHD, was raised with a lot of support, and I've tried all the apps, but have never been able to form some of the simplest (good) habits. Streaks is simple, clear (to this structurally/pattern/association oriented adhd brain), easy to stick with, and won't clutter up your task lists. I am also a retired AAA games platform/software quality control and software engineer. I can say this app is being developed by developers who take pride in their work, use their app, and understand how it needs to be used. It is not only pretty but I love the UI. It is functional and easy on the mind. You can learn a few things quickly and as someone with memory issues, encapsulating each task and the reporting access on each node is fantastic and intuitive. I look forward to new iterations and that is as someone who was a part of rapid release cycles (not that they churn you, just speaking from my perspective) who knows what that can do to the product and customers without top notch values around your users...I can honestly say, great job. Some little snippets of their attention to detail: using the wheel of your habit/task node to actively show you visual progress of a timed task. The need for positively oriented vs negatively oriented habits (don't do this, do do this). Flexibility in how you can count tasks (number of times over a period, for instance which might be good for a task like brushing a dog) that really reflect low friction ways of how people actually get things done. This reduces stress from an unnecessarily rigid structure and frees up focus and time from fiddling with the system (like rescheduling). They allow you to pause tasks as well. I use this when I'm, say, out of town and it doesn't matter if I remember to water my plants. I only wish, as someone with a need for more ongoing support in a number of tasks that the mobile version supported unlimited sheets. I did get them to add some to the desktop version, but then it syncs to my phone and I have no way of accessing the extra sheets to mark things even though I'm getting alerts for them. Oops! I understand their philosophy in not focusing on building too many habits at once, but not everyone is working with the same needs or using this to just build habits with a neurotypical makeup. So I use it differently.

Need more magic Here’s the thing about habit-tracking apps: they all promise to fix your life. Track this, check that, and suddenly—poof—you’re a productivity ninja. Habits isn’t just any app, though. It’s clean, user-friendly, and genuinely helpful. But does it have that secret sauce that keeps you coming back, day after day? Well, not quite. Let me break it down for you. What Works: 1. Simplicity That Doesn’t Insult You The interface is so intuitive, even your grandmother could use it to crush her knitting goals. No fluff, no fuss. Just pure, clean & fun design that gets out of your way. 2. Customizable Goals Without Overthinking Want to drink more water? Meditate? Remember to floss? This app lets you set your own priorities instead of forcing you into a cookie-cutter system. 3. Feedback You Can Actually Use There’s a small dopamine hit every time you check something off, and honestly, that’s what we’re all chasing, right? Where It Falls Short Here’s the kicker: Habits has everything you need—except the thing you actually need. It’s all surface-level. The app doesn’t go deep, and that’s a problem because building habits isn’t just about ticking boxes. It’s about systems. What Could Be Better: 1. Automate the “Why” Right now, the app makes you think too hard about why you’re doing what you’re doing. A James Clear-inspired feature could help link new habits to existing ones. Call it a “habit stacker” or something. 2. The magic of reps Habits misses the magic of streaks and reps—the lifeblood of habit-building. A simple feature to track and celebrate consecutive wins would make the app far more addictive. Think glowing chains or a progress bar that resets if you skip a day. Momentum matters, and without it, the app feels static, not dynamic. 3. Kill the Perfectionism Trap Miss a day? The app subtly guilt-trips you. Missing once is fine, twice not so much. The app needs to reinforce resilience, not rigid perfectionism. Final Verdict Habits is like the kid in class who always does their homework but never raises their hand. It’s solid, dependable, and you’d probably lend it your notes. But if it really wants to stand out, it needs to embrace the deeper psychology of habit formation. Until then, it’s a good tool—but not a great one. Use it, enjoy it, but don’t be afraid to break out of it Rating: 3.9 Clean, useful, but missing the heart of the matter.

Great Concept, But Needs More Solo Leveling Elements Rise: Life Reset in 66 Days is a solid app for habit-building and self-improvement, but it could be so much more immersive if it leaned further into the Solo Leveling style of gamification. Right now, the app does a decent job of tracking progress and making self-improvement feel rewarding, but it lacks the visual transformation and deep RPG mechanics that would make leveling up in real life feel as exciting as leveling up in a game. Imagine if, as you progressed, your character physically and mentally evolved—starting as a weak, untrained version of yourself and gradually transforming into a stronger, sharper, more disciplined version based on your real-life progress. Completing workouts should increase strength stats, reading should boost intelligence, and discipline-related tasks should unlock new “abilities” or perks. If Rise fully embraced the Solo Leveling concept, it could be the ultimate real-life RPG. Deeper skill trees, quests, achievements, and real-time character progression would make it way more engaging and motivating. Gamifying self-improvement is already fun, but the best way to stay motivated is to see your progress visually. If the developers make these changes, this app could become a game-changer for personal growth. Right now, it’s a great start, but I hope they push it to the next level!

Excellence in Simplicity Simple, intuitive app without much overhead that does exactly what it is intended to: Track how you do on your self-chosen way-of-life practices, every day. The red and green design encourages honesty and determination: you either accomplished your goal or you didn‘t. Focus on what’s important, don’t cheat yourself. The grouping of goals by label and the button for not-yet-updated goals are very handy and make logging take maybe half a minute for all 17 entries that I have. Starting and staying on your streaks is very rewarding and gives nice visual feedback via a chain of marked green-day entries. The length of your streak is indicated in a nice box that also shows you when you reach your self-set target streak-length. The statistics tab is well organized and contains all relevant information. It doesn‘t have many options, though, which I think is a plus because I imagine that otherwise I would spend quite some time browsing the statistics to see how well I have done. Also the minimum period that you can chose for display is six weeks, which subtly communicates to the user that this is an app for serious long-term progress (allthough I found it particularly motivating for new users as myself that you can have your first streak already on the third day and hence some early in-app sense of success). A feature worth mentioning are the well-made reminders that you can link to bring you directly to the not-yet-updated goals of a given label. I have set labels and reminders for ‚morning‘, ‚day‘ and ‚evening‘ and can then go through those list with only 1 click per item. More efficiency is impossible! The only feature I am missing - or haven‘t found yet - is to set journal entries (=goals) to inactive (or archieve them) so that you can save their statistics but don‘t have them clutter your todo list. Not every daily habit is made for eternity, like for example studying daily for some exam or doing recovery exercises till they are no longer needed. I recommend this app, it is a great tool. Use it to your benefit!

I had been really struggling in almost every aspect of my life—especially work—to get done what I needed to get done. This simple app has helped me get more done in a few weeks than I have in months, and it’s genuinely helped me so much. If I can’t get motivated to do a task, I will put it in Habitica, and that alone will help me get it done. Some things I didn’t know when I downloaded that I think would have tipped me over sooner: •You have habits, “dailies,” and to-dos. Your habits will change colors based on whether or not you do them *or* mark that you didn’t do them. This color changing alone has me 10x more likely to do a habit lol •Your to-dos change color based on how long they’ve sat in your to-do list. They turn bright red when they’re not done •You can weight the difficulty of a task I find the “getting stuff” aspect of the app less appealing, so the paywall doesn’t bug me much, though if your main motivation would be getting pets/weapons/etc, I can see how it could be troublesome. The simple color-chancing mechanic of all the sections is really effective for me. The guild feature is SUPER motivating, as well. I love joining in on quests with my guild.
